summary: Intermittent p95/p99 latency hiccups from cohort handoff delays in continuous batcher during mixed-traffic windows
description: Issue summary: Since 2026-03-12 evening, a single dedicated customer (Cerebrum Health) has reported periodic increases in tail latency (p95/p99) and occasional request timeouts while operating steady mixed-length traffic to the hosted endpoint. Impact: Intermittent 504s and p99 spikes impacting user-facing inference calls, ~0.5-1% of requests during affected windows. Environment: production, dedicated pool in us-west, models gpt-3.5-redwood-v1 and open-llm-13b. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send mixed stream of short (<=32 tokens) and long (>=512 tokens) requests from a single tenant at 60-80 qps. 2) Observe sudden p95/p99 jumps for 10-60s windows every ~7-20 minutes. Observed behavior: p95 moves from 120ms baseline to 400-1,200ms; p99 sometimes exceeds 3s and causes some client-side timeouts. Expected behavior: stable p95/p99 within documented SLOs with no periodic cliffs. Additional context: Issue first noticed after the recent continuous-batcher runtime tuning (kernel selection + handoff prioritization) deployed 2026-03-10.
comments: 2026-03-13 09:12 - Eleanor Kim (Support): Customer reported batchy tail spikes and 504s. Attached goroutine dumps and partial flamegraphs to ticket. SLA P1 escalated.

2026-03-13 10:03 - Marco Rivera (SRE): Started live traces on serving nodes in the customer's dedicated pool. Noticed repeated "cohort_handoff_wait" events aligning with p99 windows. Opening additional traces to correlate with KV cache misses.

2026-03-13 11:20 - Aisha Patel (Engineers): Looked at the batcher metrics; during events the coalescer shows a small backlog at handoff + sudden increase in serialization latency. Hypothesis: a race in handoff that inflates linger for a cohort when an idle cohort resumes and collides with active cohorts.
2026-03-13 14:45 - Support (Eleanor Kim): Customer confirmed windows coincide with their traffic shaping cron (small burst every 10 minutes). They can temporarily stop shaping on request for testing.

2026-03-14 08:05 - Marco Rivera: Deployed temporary config to reduce cohort handoff window and disable opportunistic prefix merging for the dedicated pool. Monitoring for reduction in p99. No customer-facing rollout yet.

2026-03-14 12:30 - Customer (Cerebrum Health): Observed much smaller spikes after temporary config; p99 reduced to ~700ms during prior windows. Still seeing a few outliers. Requesting root-cause and long-term fix timeline.
investigation_notes: Traces correlate p99 windows to a 50-120ms increase in batcher handoff wait + a 200-900ms increase in subsequent serialization on a subset of shards.
KV-cache hit-rate drops by ~12% for affected tenant during events, suggesting cold prefixes are being stitched during handoff.

Handoff code path shows lock contention around 'cohort_state' when a previously idle cohort attempts to merge with active micro-batches. Reproducer script built using customer's traffic pattern replicates the behavior in staging.
Telemetry: batch-size distribution shifts to higher variability during events (mix of short+long requests causes fragmented batch composition leading to delayed flushes).

Hypothesis: recent handoff prioritization change intended to favor latency for hot cohorts has an unintended starvation effect on idle->active cohorts when they resume; combined with prefix stitching increases serialization cost causing p99 cliffs.
Related PRs and runbook referenced: serving-runtime#4287, batcher design notes.
resolution: Workaround: Applied temporary runtime config to shrink cohort handoff backoff and turned off prefix opportunistic merging for Cererbrum Health's dedicated pool; customer reported reduced p99. Fix plan: engineers will patch handoff locking to avoid global contention, add explicit jitter on cohort resume, and improve hot/cohort priority heuristic. Patch PR target: github.com/redwood-inference/continuous-batcher/pull/238 (in review). Rollout: staged to 10% of dedicated pools for 24h, then full. Follow-ups: add unit/regression tests for resume path, add an observability alert for 'cohort_handoff_wait' > 100ms sustained. ETA for full fix: 2026-03-20.
postmortem_follow_up_actions: Add e2e synthetic test that mashes short+long requests with idle-resume pattern to CI (owner: Aisha Patel, due: 2026-03-19)
Patch handoff locking to use per-cohort fine-grained locks (owner: Marco Rivera, PR in review, due: 2026-03-18)
Instrument and alert on cohort_handoff_wait > 100ms in prod (owner: Observability team, due: 2026-03-16)
Update customer-facing KB with recommended traffic shaping knobs for dedicated pools (owner: Support, due: 2026-03-22)
